title: Derive the Pi stage tool gate from the write guard's own rule
action: Make the stage-tools hook take its write-open verdict from the write guard instead of its own list. Today run_inner builds `is_after_gate` from a hand-kept four-phase match and then sets `execution_is_open = (!is_gated && is_after_gate) || gate_approved`. That list disagrees with `write_guard::is_gated_phase`, which gates only `exploring` and `planning`, so `grooming`, `idle` and `compounding-complete` wrongly come back read-only. Replace the whole computation with `execution_is_open = !is_gated_phase(phase) || gate_approved` and delete `is_after_gate`. Extract the mapping into one pure function, `pub(crate) fn allowed_tools_for(phase: &str, gate_approved: bool) -> &'static [&'static str]`, and have run_inner call it, so the rule is testable without stdout capture. Do not change READ_ONLY_TOOLS or FULL_TOOL_SET: the eight names are exactly Pi's eight built-in tools. Do not change the JSON key set the hook prints — the Pi belt reads `stage`, `stage_name`, `allowed_tools`, `user_message`/`user_notice` and `model_message`/`model_notice`, and dropping any of them breaks the belt. Keep the hook advisory: it still fails open and still returns SUCCESS on every path. Work RED FIRST: add the failing cases before the fix and record the red output. The existing test `stage_tools_decision_logic` asserts the `is_after_gate` local you are deleting; that is a structure assertion, so replace it with behavior assertions over `allowed_tools_for` rather than repairing it. Keep `stage_tools_returns_read_only_in_planning_phase_without_gate` and `stage_tools_fails_open_without_bee_store` working as they are.

truths: grooming, idle and compounding-complete return the full tool set when the execution gate is unapproved
exploring and planning still return read,bash when the execution gate is unapproved
an approved execution gate still returns the full tool set in every phase
the hook's printed JSON keys are unchanged, so the Pi belt still parses it
the phase-to-tools rule has one home and is derived from write_guard::is_gated_phase

artifacts.substantive: allowed_tools_for derived from is_gated_phase, is_after_gate deleted, behavior tests covering all nine known phases at both gate states

judge_obligation_ack: Tiny lane kept, but the independent read is NOT skipped: an independent bee-review worker reads this diff against the write-guard rule before the cap. The change deletes a duplicate rule rather than adding guard logic, and the hook stays advisory (D5: tool_call is the only blocking surface).

mistakes.wrong: The plan's whole rationale said write_guard 'permits writes' in idle and compounding-complete. It does not: is_terminal_phase plus GATE_ALLOWED_PREFIXES_INTAKE refuse a terminal-phase write outside .bee/, docs/, plans/ and AGENTS.md, and an unrecognized phase is refused for every write. I read is_gated_phase and stopped, never sweeping the other phase predicates in the same file.
mistakes.better: Before claiming one predicate IS a rule, grep the file for every sibling predicate on the same input (is_terminal_phase, is_known_phase sat 4 lines above is_gated_phase) and read each call site.

mistakes.wrong: I wrote the corrected allowed_tools_for body in the same edit that extracted the function, so the first test run would have been green-on-arrival; I had to paste the old rule back to earn a real red.
mistakes.better: Extract as a behavior-preserving refactor first, watch the new tests fail, then change the rule: one edit per intent.

mistakes.wrong: I wrote `--lib hooks::stage_tools` into the cell's verify at plan time without ever running it; the bee crate ships only a bin target, so the approved proof command was unrunnable and the cap refused.
mistakes.better: Run the verify command once at plan time, before it goes into the cell packet, so an approved proof is a proof that executes.
